prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System (CBTC): underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering. Operations Control Centre: Line Traffic Controller owns service regulation, assesses passenger/recovery impacts, verifies approved timetable revisions. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern), non-vital, sends Crew Login Token Bundle; presents options before confirmation. Service Timetable Server supplies schedules; approved-change-workflow only. Passenger Information Gateway receives operational service state; distributes aligned approved platform/destination messages, protection-isolated. Voice Dispatch Console: verbal instructions require Revenue Train Operator readback; cannot replace safety validation. Operator owns readiness/compliance; reports condition/cab/passenger/local hazards. Maintenance Diagnostic Server supplies non-vital trends to Signal Maintenance Engineer, who advises recovery, not regulation.
North District Zone Controller (Marble)/South District Zone Controller (Orchid): northern/southern mainlines/turnbacks; East Junction Interlocking (Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking approaches. Interlockings send vital point/occupancy/locking states, retain locking/release authority. Zones preserve separation; authority requires proved/locked points, overlap/flank/conflict protection; boundaries require route/points/vacancy. Mismatch/lost correspondence restricts authority within braking envelope; conflicting axle-counter evidence resolves restrictively. Falcon sends Axle Counter Reset Request; routes/approaches inhibit reset. Maple (unidentified) verifies/records clearance. West sends Route Release Exception List; hazards persist until excluded.
Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): initialization/protected-manual/automatic/fallback/cutout; validates messages, enforces authority/speed/doors/braking; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer divergence degrades separation. Transfers require position/receiving-zone validation; isolation/brake feedback assured. Train Radio Modem reports connectivity. Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron) sends Radio Handover Audit File; degradation retains validated authority. Safety Data Communication Network: segregated/authenticated/integrity-protected deterministic messaging; sends Clock Drift Sample Report to Cryptographic Key Management Appliance for clock/certificate-tolerance verification; appliance produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack under approved maintenance window, records reference. Cyber Security Officer reviews changes/access/authentication anomalies before reliance.
Post-incident/degradation/timetable authority reviews reconcile interlocking/intent/response. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot: closed/locked/bypassed/inhibited/faulted. Door/direction compatibility gates departure; Marble suppresses unsafe-berth authority.

Document units:
S133: Station status indications presented to local station staff are derived from validated CBTC states rather than from unverified field contacts alone.
S134: These indications distinguish normal service, held train, door interlock fault, radio degraded, emergency stop active, and evacuation support conditions.
S135: The Metro Operations Control System displays station and platform states with the same identifiers used in controller workstations to reduce interpretation errors during incidents.
S136: Passenger Information Gateway receives train prediction data, stopping pattern changes, and platform allocation updates after the CBTC system has reconciled them with the active timetable.
S137: The Passenger Information Gateway shall not publish a revised destination or skip-stop message until the underlying train identity and route have been confirmed by the CBTC system.
S138: When a platform is taken out of service, the passenger information interface marks the affected train movements as unavailable for boarding while retaining their operational tracking in the control center.
S139: Service Timetable Server provides planned service context used to compare predicted arrivals against scheduled platform usage.
S140: Metro Operations Control System coordinates timetable deviation, platform closure, and station crowding information before it is released to passenger-facing systems.
S141: Voice Dispatch Console displays train calling identity, current platform association, and the latest operational hold reason so that spoken instructions match automated indications.
S142: The Line Traffic Controller may apply a station hold through dispatch controls, and the hold is reflected in CBTC departure logic without changing the underlying route locking rules.
S143: Dispatch-related controls use positive confirmation and cancellation states so that a cancelled hold is not confused with a timeout, failed message, or rejected command.
S144: Kestrel shall report train door enable side, berth identity, and departure readiness to support platform interface checks during dwell and dispatch.
S145: Saffron shall maintain message delivery paths for station interface traffic during normal radio coverage transitions and degraded coverage recovery.
S146: Train Radio Modem uses the Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack before accepting renewed secure sessions for passenger-facing and station-interface data paths.
S147: Safety Data Communication Network carries safety-relevant station interface messages separately from nonvital passenger information messages.
S148: Maintenance Diagnostic Server records station interface faults, rejected commands, and inconsistent indications for later investigation by the Signal Maintenance Engineer.
S149: Cyber Security Officer reviews access rights for passenger information and dispatch integration workstations when station-facing interfaces are commissioned or materially changed.
